content: Quinidine is an oral medication primarily used to treat life-threatening arrhythmias, as it helps make the heart more resistant to abnormal electrical activity. It is also prescribed for the treatment of malaria. However, studies have indicated that certain antiarrhythmic drugs, including quinidine, may increase the risk of death, particularly in individuals who have experienced a prior heart attack. Therefore, quinidine is typically reserved for severe cases. Quinidine is available in tablet form and is taken by mouth. The immediate-release version is usually taken three to four times daily, while the extended-release version is taken two to three times daily. Extended-release tablets must be swallowed whole and should not be cut, crushed, or chewed. It is essential to follow the prescription instructions carefully and not to take more or less of the medication than prescribed. Quinidine helps manage the condition but does not cure it, so it is important to continue taking it even if you feel well. Do not stop taking quinidine without consulting your doctor. Before starting quinidine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to quinidine, quinine, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription drugs you are taking, including anticoagulants (e.g. Notify your doctor if you have an infection or a history of myasthenia gravis, heart disease, kidney disease, liver disease, or muscle weakness. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor immediately. If you become pregnant while taking quinidine, contact your doctor. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking quinidine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate drowsiness caused by quinidine, so it is advisable to limit alcohol consumption. Additionally, discuss with your doctor the use of cigarettes and caffeine-containing beverages, as these may increase heart irritability and interfere with quinidine's effectiveness. Do not switch brands of quinidine without consulting your doctor. Avoid consuming grapefruit juice while taking quinidine, as it may interact with the medication. Do not alter the amount of salt in your diet without first discussing it with your doctor. If you miss a dose of quinidine, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Quinidine may cause side effects. Minor side effects include diarrhea, stomach pain or cramps, dizziness, lightheadedness, headache, fatigue, weakness, rash, vision changes, difficulty sleeping, and tremors. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention. These include irregular heartbeat, chest pain, skin rash, hearing changes (such as ringing or hearing loss), vision changes (such as blurred vision or light sensitivity), and unusual bleeding or bruising. If you experience any of these, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store quinidine in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as regular monitoring is necessary to evaluate your response to quinidine. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Quinidine is sold under several brand names, including Cardioquin®, Quinaglute Dura-Tabs®, Quinidex Extentabs®, and Quinora®.
